title: FP8 weirdness — repro playbook and breadcrumbs
body:
Summary:
- Scratchpad for a reproducible playbook of intermittent NaN/Inf/quality regressions seen when running `--quantize fp8` on a 7B-style transformer (decoder-only) in the serving runtime.
- Symptoms: model returns NaN logits or output contains repeated <nan> tokens after ~40-180 tokens. Intermittent: sometimes fine, sometimes blows up mid-generation. More common with long context (>512) and when batching mixed sequence lengths.

Environment notes (observed combinations):
- PyTorch 2.2.0 + CUDA 12.1 + cuDNN 8.9 on A100 (DGX-ish infra)
- Torch nightly experiments (2025-01) also tested — same symptom but different reproducibility
- Serving runtime: custom C++ kernels + torchscript wrapper (local debug build)
- Quantization pipeline: FP8 calibration (blockwise, per-channel scale) -> export to runtime format -> runtime uses FP8 kernels with fused softmax/attention
- Also tried on CPU (AVX2) emulation path of FP8: does NOT reproduce there (suspect GPU kernel/warp level issue)

Quick repro (minimal):
1) Checkout repro branch: git checkout repro/fp8-bug-432
2) Conda env: conda activate ri-infer-debug
3) Run (example):
   CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python tools/repro/run_generation.py
     --model-path checkpoints/7b-fp8-calib/
     --quantize fp8
     --batch 1
     --prompt-file tests/prompt-long.txt
     --max-len 1024
     --seed 1234

Observed output snippet (truncated) from failed run:
--- LOG ---
[2025-02-14 13:02:11,112] INFO: start generation (seq=1024)
[2025-02-14 13:02:12,001] DEBUG: attention-kernel: launch (B=1, S=896, H=32)
[2025-02-14 13:02:12,104] ERROR: numeric check: found +inf in softmax input (layer=7, head=21, pos=412)
[2025-02-14 13:02:12,105] ERROR: logits contain nan -> aborting generation
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tools/repro/run_generation.py", line 214, in <module>
    out = generator.generate(batch)
  File "../runtime/generator.py", line 87, in generate
    out = CppRuntime.forward(inputs)
RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered (attention_kernel.cu:432)
--- END LOG ---

Commands I ran to get more context:
- nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE --format=csv
- python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory)"
- export TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1 (did not give more useful trace in custom kernel)
- CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python ... -> makes crash deterministic but only shows top-level device assert, not the kernel line number in our code
- gdb attach (nvprof replacement): cuda-gdb attach <pid>, set breakpoint in attention_kernel -> stepping sometimes shows numeric overflow on reduction
- instrumented kernels with printf: observed extremely large intermediate values in the exponent before softmax (e.g. >1e20)

Quick diffs that change behavior:
- Re-run exact same command but change seed -> different replicate (sometimes passes, sometimes fails)
- Reduce prompt length to <=512 -> passes reliably
- Disable batching or set uniform sequence lengths -> passes more reliably
- Switch to BF16 calibration (instead of FP8) -> passes (no NaNs)
- Emulation/CPU FP8 path -> passes
- Run with `--disable-kv-cache` -> passes (suspect KV cache accumulation or stale scales)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Per-layer/per-head scale drift: calibration scales for blockwise FP8 are stale when KV cache causes different activation distributions at generation-time vs calibration-time -> exponent overflow in attention softmax.
2) Race/atomic bug in custom kernel causing occasional miswritten scale or scratch memory corruption under mixed seq lengths -> results in +inf before softmax.
3) Reduction numerical instability due to fused kernels doing in-kernel exponent accumulation in FP8/FP16 mix (e.g., accumulating exp in FP16 without proper winograd-like scaling).
4) Improper handling of padding/masking in fused attention when sequences are batched with variable lengths -> some positions get very large logits.
5) Bug in quant-dequant path where INT8/FP8 compressed values are not zeroed on cache reuse -> garbage in attention input.

What I've tried (detailed):
- Re-calibration on the same data but forcing different strategies:
  - per-tensor scale vs per-channel: per-channel reduces failure rate slightly but does not eliminate it
  - block-size 64 vs 128: smaller block-size reduces regressions (fewer NaNs)
- Insert numeric guards in kernel:
  - clamp(exp_in) to +- 1e4 before exp() -> immediate reduction in NaNs but still see degraded distribution (quality loss)
  - add atomic initialization of scratch buffers -> slightly lower incidence
- Add assertions in Python runtime to check for inf/nan after each major op (attention, layernorm, FFN). Failure is caught earliest in attention.
- Tried pytorch.autograd.set_detect_anomaly(True) on CPU emulation path -> no anomalies (because GPU kernel is native)

Representative kernel printf snippet (from instrumented dev build):
[ATTN kernel] layer=7 head=21 pos=412 q_val=2.1e+03 k_val=-5.2e+02 dot=1.2e+25 scale=1.234e-04 -> exp_in = dot * scale = 1.48e+21
Note: exp(1.48e+21) overflow -> produced +inf and downstream NaN after softmax normalization.

Quick mitigation (for customer-facing):
- Fallback policy: if quantize=fp8 and sequence_length>512, route request to bf16 model variant (runtime routing rule). Implement as hotfix in orchestration.
- Disable KV cache for FP8 served variant (loss of perf but prevents NaNs).
- Add on-the-fly numeric sanitizer: if any +inf detected in attention input, clip to safe_win (e.g., +-50) and continue; log detailed telemetry for offline analysis.

Instrumentation to add (next):
- Track per-request: max(abs(attn_input)), percent of elements > threshold, first-layer/first-head stats. Emit to console and to queryable traces.
- Save snapshot of problematic KV cache segments (serialize raw fp8 blocks) to S3 for offline repro.
- Add kernel-level guard that zeroes scratch/temporary memory at launch to detect stale memory bugs.
- Add an option to force FP8 emulation path on GPU (slower) to compare behavior deterministically.

Repro experiments planned:
- Controlled grid:
  - vary context length: [128, 256, 512, 768, 1024]
  - batch shape: [1x1024, 2x(512,256), 4x(256,256,256,256)]
  - calibration mode: per-tensor/per-channel/block-size
  - kv_cache: enabled/disabled
  - seed: repeat 8 seeds per config
- Capture deterministic traces via CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and kernel printf for failing runs only.

Notes / breadcrumbs from other folks:
- Samir: "saw similar on 8/2024 but blamed float exp overflow in fused softmax; we added clamp but that hides bad quant scale"
- Lina: "my quick hack was to re-run calibration with generation-like sequences (longer context) and that reduced failures by ~60%"
- Link to earlier thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C01ABCDEF/p1671234567890

What I need help with (ask):
- Kernel code owner: can you review attention_kernel reduction path for any non-deterministic memory writes? (cc @kernel-team)
- Math lead: thoughts on safe rescaling strategies for attention (row-wise max-subtract before exp) that are numerically stable with FP8 quantized inputs?
- SRE: can we provision a debug node with persistent nvprof/cuda-gdb and larger logging retention so we can collect full device traces on failing runs?

Quick checklist to reproduce reliably (for you):
- Use the repro branch, set CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1, max-len=1024, seed=1234, quantize=fp8, batch shapes mixing long/short sequences, run until failure or 8 seeds tried.
- If fail: copy logs and kernel printf dump to s3://ri-repro/fp8-432/<timestamp>/ and paste link to Jira ticket JIRA-ML-987.

Closing note:
- Appears to be interaction between quantization scales + KV cache + fused attention kernel numerics on GPU. Prioritize quick mitigation (routing to BF16 or disabling KV for FP8 variants) while we root cause the kernel-level behavior.

Raw command history (copied from shell history) - useful for exact reproduction:
- git checkout repro/fp8-bug-432
- conda activate ri-infer-debug
- export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1
- python tools/repro/run_generation.py --model-path checkpoints/7b-fp8-calib/ --quantize fp8 --batch 1 --prompt-file tests/prompt-long.txt --max-len 1024 --seed 1234
- python tools/repro/run_generation.py --model-path checkpoints/7b-bf16/ --quantize bf16 --batch 1 --prompt-file tests/prompt-long.txt --max-len 1024 --seed 1234
- python tools/dbg/collect_kernel_dump.py --pid 12345 --out /tmp/kernel-dump.txt

If anything here is unclear ping me in slack @nadia or add notes on JIRA.

-- Nadia
